checks: Eight original main-text Theorems3.1,3.3,3.4,3.5,3.6,4.1(Chatterjee),4.5,4.11 independently enumerated by bold font and visually compared. Section2 Propositions and all Lemmas are excluded as inventory claims. Main text ends24; appendix bodies beginning25 are excluded.

Twenty-four entries preserve original convex regression classes, design/model assumptions, losses, affine-distance class, grid-partition class, referenced Lemma3.2 approximation, covering/bracketing conventions and local objective/radius. Eleven auxiliary passages retain standing constants and proof-only context. Lemma3.2 is a source passage identifying the function in3.6, not an invented definition or theorem.

Independent source-clause graph verifies56 direct uses and64 related-theorem connections. Fixed-design rates inherit2.2 explicitly via3.2. Theorem4.1 keeps its own arbitrary deterministic design and convex class;4.5 and4.11 are deterministic entropy statements. No proof-only Gaussian-supremum or entropy requirements are imposed on the rate theorems. Only3.6 requires the Lemma3.2 function.

Fourteen source notes preserve fraktur notation, model independence and LSE attainment conventions, normalized-body volume error, slab/facet and grid/cell distinctions, affine-distance interpretation, nonunique lemma function, h-uniformity, bracketing-scale endpoint and distinct metrics. Source formulas are not silently repaired.

All24 entries retain exact author keywords, source headings/kinds and matching selectors. All64 connections have a checked paper-local path and a source-specific explanation. Names are natural-language source terms; notation is preserved in statements and selectors.

All six content JSONs reproduce byte for byte in a fresh empty directory. Seven retained scripts support generation and separate inventory/full-source review. Rebuilding is not a new semantic PDF review.

The census preserves source statements and context rather than certifying theorem truth. The selected function in3.6 is identified only by the main-text existential lemma; its appendix construction remains unresolved and outside scope. Potential source defects are recorded separately.

source_notes.note: Registered arXiv2006.02044v2,67pages,stamp3Sep2024. Main text ends24; appendix begins25. Preserve this registered version and its eight theorem environments, not an abstract or replaced published source.

Fraktur L in9/3.3 differs from Lipschitz L; fraktur B_d denotes the Euclidean unit ball. Population law and empirical measure are blackboard P and P_n; classes and grid are calligraphic. PDF plain text conflates these fonts; checked rendered pages and font metadata.

Model1 gives iid Gaussian errors without explicitly stating independence from random design. This is a usual model convention needed for conditional Gaussian calculations. LSE2 chooses any minimizer; generic existence, measurable selection and off-design uniqueness are not guaranteed by that notation.

Theorem4.1 assumes a convex class F, not necessarily a class of convex functions. It does not explicitly impose closedness of evaluation vectors. For the open convex family of constant functions c in(0,1), minimizers can fail when the sample mean is outside this interval. Preserve source wording and record missing attainment/closure conditions; do not assert theorem truth from transcription checks.

Containment in the Euclidean unit ball does not imply volume<=1 as stated after3. Retain the actual domain condition without adding the claimed volume consequence as a hypothesis. Theorem4.5 explicitly needs only containment, and4.1 binds an arbitrary convex body.

F in14 counts slabs, while3.1 explicitly bounds facets. They are not the same literal count. Constants may depend on dimension and the stated complexity bounds; do not replace a fixed-dimensional slab condition with an unrestricted growing-polytope sequence.

n equals the number of grid points inOmega; delta is small enough for16 and n>=2. C_(k,h) partitions grid intersections, not necessarily every point ofOmega. Referring to slab format14 for cells does not require each cell to contain a dimensional ball. Integer k,h and cell endpoint assignment conventions remain implicit.

F^frakturL bounds the unsquared empirical distance to all affine functions. It is design-dependent and allows unbounded affine trends. Do not substitute a Lipschitz bound, uniform bound, or a squared-distance threshold. The supremum class and the unrestricted estimator class are different.

Lemma3.2 provides existence of a convex tilde f_k with at most C_d*k simplex pieces and approximation properties; it does not uniquely define a function. Theorem3.6 calls it the function from that lemma. Preserve the reference and existential properties; no unique constructor or all-witness assertion is supplied from the excluded appendix. Small-k meaning of(1-C_d*k^(-1/d))*Omega is also retained without correction.

Theorem3.5 says C_d depends on d alone for every k,h>=1 and writes(log n)^h. The proof-sketch bounds47–48 have powers(cd log n)^h, potentially hiding h-dependent factors if h varies. Preserve the printed theorem and flag the stated constant scope rather than silently importing h-dependence.

Theorem4.5 states the bound for every0<epsilon<Gamma with log(Gamma/epsilon)^(d+1). For fixed t large enough to include constants -Gamma and Gamma onOmega=[-1,1] and one simplex equalOmega, their Lp distance exceedsGamma, so the bracketing entropy stays at least log2 as epsilon approachesGamma, whereas the printed RHS tends to0. A restricted epsilon range or a log convention may be intended, but none is specified in the main-text constants convention. Preserve43 and record this endpoint issue without correcting it.

Population squared L2, empirical squared L2, unnormalized Lebesgue Lp and normalized discrete Lp are distinct. Full-function empirical distances are pseudometrics until quotienting evaluation vectors. Covering entropy uses closed balls; bracket endpoints are pointwise ordered functions with metric width. Centers/quotient conventions are implicit; finite-dimensional metric facts are ambient, not theorem-truth checks.

The p range1<=p<infinity and small-delta grid convention precede4.11 rather than appearing in its first sentence. Keep this context without rewriting the original. Constant c_(d,p) occurs inside an F-th power, unlike4.5 where k appears linearly. No response noise belongs to this entropy theorem.

The discussion proposes bounded-density random design with changed constants, unbounded designs, non-Gaussian errors and modified interior loss. These are not replacement hypotheses or new inventoried Theorems; Gaussian errors and original losses remain the census scope.

ambient_resolution.T3.1: Gaussian convex regression1; uniform random design and population squared L2 loss4; expectation over all observations. Normalized domain3. First branch is bounded-Lipschitz class with B>=L or Lipschitz-only class, lower constant sigma L and threshold N_(d,sigma/L). Second branch requires dimensional facet bound and uses bounded-only class, sigma B and N_(d,sigma/B). Its piecewise-affine witness, Gaussian supremum, entropy bounds and Theorem4.1 are proof-only, not hypotheses.
ambient_resolution.T3.3: Section3.2 explicitly imports Section2.2: Gaussian model, regular small-delta grid, normalized slab polytope and dimensional F bound. F^frakturL is empirical distance at most frakturL to all affine functions; the estimator is unrestricted convex LSE. Empirical squared risk. Preserve all three dimension cases and constants/threshold; frakturL is not Lipschitz L.
ambient_resolution.T3.4: Same fixed-design setup as3.3. Supremum runs over simultaneous L-bounded L-Lipschitz convex functions, whereas estimator ranges over all convex functions. Positive sigma,L; n>=C_(d,sigma/L). Neither3.6 nor the selected Lemma3.2 function is required to state this supremum bound.
ambient_resolution.T3.5: Same fixed-design setup. C_(k,h) is defined by a grid partition into k convex regions each cut by at most h slabs, with affine restriction of f. It does not require full-region disjointness or impose normalized-domain inradius on each region. Preserve d<=3, d=4 and d>=5 rates; k,h are counts although theorem writes only >=1. Uniformity of C_d in h is retained as stated.
ambient_resolution.T3.6: Same fixed-design setup and unrestricted convex LSE with empirical risk. The true function is specifically the tilde f_k referred to in Lemma3.2, whose full main-text statement is archived. Keep n>=N_d and 1<=k<=min(sqrt(n)*sigma^(-d/4),c_d*n), including the sigma dependence. The existential lemma does not uniquely select this function; appendix construction is outside scope.
ambient_resolution.T4.1: Own fixed deterministic design in arbitrary convex body X, not necessarily a lattice or normalized Omega. The class F is convex as a set of functions; its individual functions need not be convex. Gaussian noises and f inF are inline hypotheses. Generic LSE2 and empirical loss8, H_f expected localized Gaussian supremum minus t²/2, t_f its maximizing radius. Both probability/expectation bounds and inequalities28–29 belong to the statement. Measurable minimizer existence/closedness is not stated for an arbitrary convex class.
ambient_resolution.T4.5: Deterministic entropy theorem for a convex domain inside the unit ball, Gamma-bounded convex center, and Gamma-bounded convex functions within unnormalized Lebesgue Lp distance t on allOmega. Simplices have disjoint interiors and center affine on each; their union need not equalOmega. Brackets use Lp on the union, for1<=p<infinity. No random design, Gaussian noise, normalized inradius3, lattice, or Lemma3.2 approximation is imposed. Printed log(Gamma/epsilon) bound is retained despite a large-epsilon endpoint concern.
ambient_resolution.T4.11: Deterministic covering entropy under the discrete normalized Lp metric51,1<=p<infinity from preceding prose, grid15 with n=cardinality and small delta16, normalized slab polytope14 and3, dimensional F. No Gaussian response/model, continuous population loss, affine approximant, or bracketing condition is required. Preserve [c_(d,p) log(1/delta)]^F (t/epsilon)^(d/2) for every positive epsilon,t.
